problem: Find the equation of the right-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(-4,-3)$ and passes through the point $(1,2).$

feedback.problem: Find the equation of the right-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(-4,0)$ and passes through the point $(2,6).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(-4,0),$ we substitute $h=-4$ and $k=0$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(2,6),$ so we can substitute $x=2$ and $y=6$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x+4) \\ {6}^{2} & =4p(2+4) \\ 36 & =24p \\ p & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x+4) \\ {y}^{2} & =4(\frac{3}{2})(x+4) \\ {y}^{2} & =6(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$
